verses.1: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
verses.2: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
verses.3: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,
verses.4: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
verses.5:
Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! + 9:5 Or forever blessed Amen.
 God’s Sovereign Choice
 ( Genesis 25:19–28|GEN 25:19-28 ; Malachi 1:1–5|MAL 1:1-5 )
verses.6: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
verses.7: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.” + 9:7 Genesis 21:12|GEN 21:12
verses.8: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
verses.9: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.” + 9:9 Genesis 18:14|GEN 18:14
verses.10: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
verses.11: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
verses.12: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.” + 9:12 Genesis 25:23|GEN 25:23
verses.13: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.” + 9:13 Malachi 1:2–3|MAL 1:2-3
verses.14: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
verses.15:
For He says to Moses:
 “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy,
 and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.” + 9:15 Exodus 33:19|EXO 33:19
verses.16: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
verses.17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.” + 9:17 Exodus 9:16|EXO 9:16 (see also LXX)
verses.18: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
verses.19: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
verses.20: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?” + 9:20 Isaiah 29:16|ISA 29:16 ; Isaiah 45:9
verses.21: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
verses.22: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
verses.23: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory —
verses.24: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
verses.25:
As He says in Hosea:
 “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people,
 and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,” + 9:25 Hosea 2:23|HOS 2:23
verses.26:
and,
 “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them,
 ‘You are not My people,’
 they will be called
 ‘sons of the living God.’” + 9:26 Hosea 1:10|HOS 1:10
verses.27:
Isaiah cries out concerning Israel:
 “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea,
 only the remnant will be saved.
verses.28:
For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth
 thoroughly and decisively.” + 9:28 Isaiah 10:22–23|ISA 10:22-23 (see also LXX)
verses.29:
It is just as Isaiah foretold:
 “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants,
 we would have become like Sodom,
 we would have resembled Gomorrah.” + 9:29 Isaiah 1:9|ISA 1:9 (see also LXX) 
 Israel’s Unbelief
verses.30: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
verses.31: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
verses.32: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,
verses.33:
as it is written:
 “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling
 and a rock of offense; + 9:33 Isaiah 8:14|ISA 8:14 
 and the one who believes in Him
 will never be put to shame.” + 9:33 Isaiah 28:16|ISA 28:16 (see also LXX)
